REVISES: configs/gate_answer_probe_cost_v1_design.json (frozen 2f59f6a). V1.0's PHASE_0 utility and PHASE_5 criterion are SUPERSEDED. Everything else in V1.0 -- the cost definition, the instrumentation-gap disclosure, the family/label-correlation limitation, the mandatory diagnostics, the model ladder, the train/calibration/eval separation, and the fresh-split requirement -- is carried forward UNCHANGED.
WHY_REVISED: V1.0 froze a strictly-lexicographic scalar U = Q - EPSILON*C/C_REF. PHASE_3 showed this bounds the maximum attainable Delta_U_gate at EPSILON * (max token saving) / C_REF ~= 0.0006, so even a perfect oracle beats the best fixed policy by only +0.0007 -- unresolvable by a grouped bootstrap. It also makes accepting irrational for any fitted classifier (a false ACCEPT forfeits 1.0 quality; a correct ACCEPT saves 0.0006), which is why P3 correctly converged to always-escalate. This is a mathematical property of the lexicographic choice, derivable from the frozen definition a priori, and was a protocol-design error rather than a data-dependent discovery. Full record: RESEARCH_STATUS.json answer_probe_cost_gate_v1.DESIGN_FLAW_IDENTIFIED_IN_THE_FROZEN_UTILITY.
WHAT_IS_NOT_BEING_DONE: EPSILON is not retuned. The lambda_T sensitivity grid is not promoted to a criterion. No exchange rate between a quality point and a compute unit is invented. The V1.0 numbers are not re-reported as a result. The preference ordering itself is UNCHANGED -- 'maximize quality; among quality-tied policies prefer the cheaper action' -- this revision only changes how that same ordering is OPERATIONALIZED for a statistical test.
PARAMETER_CHOICE_DISCIPLINE: Every parameter introduced here is being chosen AFTER PHASE_3 results were seen. That ordering cannot be undone, so each is instead set in the direction that makes promotion HARDER than the natural or precedented choice would be. Each entry below states its precedent and why the chosen value is stricter. If the gate passes under these values, it passes despite the ordering rather than because of it.

PHASE_0_PRIME_OPERATIONALIZATION.decision_rule: ESCALATE if P_hat(memory improves quality) >= TAU, else ACCEPT. A single learned score with one operating point -- the same model class as V1.0's P3, not a more complex one.
PHASE_0_PRIME_OPERATIONALIZATION.why_this_is_the_same_preference_ordering: 'Prefer the cheaper action among quality-tied policies' is exactly a constrained optimization: maximize compute saved subject to quality being preserved. Expressing it as a constraint rather than folding it into one scalar is what removes the need for an exchange rate, and it is what makes the effect size (compute saved) large enough for a bootstrap to resolve.
PHASE_0_PRIME_OPERATIONALIZATION.TAU_selection_rule: TAU is chosen on the CALIBRATION partition ONLY, as the value that MAXIMIZES mean compute saved SUBJECT TO calibration quality loss vs always-escalate being <= TAU_SELECTION_BUDGET. Never chosen on TRAIN (overfits) or EVAL (invalidates the one-shot test).

AMENDMENT_2026-08-10T23:55Z_tau_selectio.what_changed: TAU selection now targets a calibration quality loss of 0.01 (= QUALITY_NONINFERIORITY_MARGIN / 2) instead of the full 0.02 margin.
AMENDMENT_2026-08-10T23:55Z_tau_selectio.why: Selecting the argmax exactly AT a constraint boundary estimated from finite calibration data is a maximum-likelihood point estimate with zero headroom, so it violates that constraint out-of-sample roughly half the time. That is a textbook property of boundary selection, derivable without reference to any observed number, and it is what the first development run exhibited (calibration loss <= 0.02 by construction, holdout loss 0.0345). Reserving half the margin as generalization headroom is the standard remedy.
AMENDMENT_2026-08-10T23:55Z_tau_selectio.direction_of_effect: This makes the selected policy MORE conservative -- fewer ACCEPTs, less compute saved -- so it makes C2_material_compute_reduction HARDER to pass. It does not loosen any promotion criterion.
AMENDMENT_2026-08-10T23:55Z_tau_selectio.what_did_NOT_change: All five PHASE_5' promotion criteria are untouched: margin 0.02, minimum relative reduction 0.10, positive LCB, safety bound 0.30, class floors 40/40. Only the development-side estimator that picks an operating point was corrected.
AMENDMENT_2026-08-10T23:55Z_tau_selectio.why_this_is_legitimate_iteration: exec_training_v2 is explicitly marked diagnosis_only / hypothesis_generation_only in its SPLIT_LINEAGE.json. Improving a controller and its operating-point estimator using development data is exactly what development data is for. What must not move -- and has not -- are the promotion criteria and the requirement that the decisive test run exactly once against a split that has never been touched. This is nonetheless the SECOND post-hoc revision in this study and is recorded as such rather than folded in silently.

C1_quality_non_inferiority.precedent_and_why_stricter: This project's previously frozen margins are 0.03 (HRM confirmation H2-H0) and 0.05 (EOB ExecutiveOpportunity; subgroup safety tolerance; SCALE_TOLERANCE). 0.02 is tighter than every one of them, so the margin cannot be characterized as loosened to accommodate a result already seen. In absolute terms it permits the gate to give up at most 2 quality points per 100 tasks against a ~0.39 baseline.

C2_material_compute_reduction.why_a_floor_rather_than_just_greater_tha: A statistically-positive but operationally trivial saving (P3's realized 1.8% in PHASE_3) would not justify deploying a learned gate at all. Requiring >=10% is strictly harder to pass than 'any positive reduction', and remains far below the 40% the oracle demonstrates is attainable, so it is a deployment-relevance floor rather than a bar set at the observed effect.

C3_compute_reduction_is_statistically_re.metric: grouped-bootstrap 2.5% LCB of the per-task token saving (best fixed policy minus candidate) > 0, resampled by family
C3_compute_reduction_is_statistically_re.note: Same resampling convention as every prior gate in this project (scripts.diagnose_c5_confirmation_stopgate.grouped_lcb).

C4_safety_bound.status: CARRIED OVER UNCHANGED from configs/gate_answer_probe_v2_design.json, where it was frozen before any V2 data existed. Retained for continuity, though C1 is expected to bind first and much harder: at the ~26% memory-better rate observed in development, a 0.02 quality margin implies this rate must actually stay below roughly 0.076. Keeping both means the stricter constraint governs.

C5_eval_class_floors.if_unmet: INCONCLUSIVE_INSUFFICIENT_EVAL_CLASS_SUPPORT. Do not reshuffle, do not relax.

PHASE_5_PRIME_PROMOTION_CRITERIA.if_not_met: Report as a formal negative result. Do not retune TAU, the margin, the reduction floor, or the model after seeing the evaluation result. A failure here closes cost-aware confidence-only gating on this instrument.

CONTROLLER_MUST_BE_REFIT.why: V1.0's P3 was fit against the compressed lexicographic objective and therefore learned to always-escalate -- optimal under that objective, useless under this one. Testing it unchanged would evaluate a controller optimized for a criterion that has been withdrawn.
CONTROLLER_MUST_BE_REFIT.what_is_permitted: Refitting on the CONSUMED exec_training_v2 development data is permitted: that split's SPLIT_LINEAGE.json allows diagnosis_only / hypothesis_generation_only, and controller design is hypothesis generation. No promotion claim may be made from it.
CONTROLLER_MUST_BE_REFIT.what_is_forbidden: Refitting, or reselecting TAU, on the fresh evaluation split. PHASE_5 loads the frozen controller and TAU and computes the five criteria exactly once.
